sentences.zh: 工作职责以外的事情，这样我就不用去干本职工作了。

sentences.en: So I think just before we met, I was working for Argos head office, and I really enjoyed my colleagues, we had such a great time,
sentences.zh: 所以我想就在我们认识之前，我曾在阿戈斯（Argos）总公司工作，我真的很喜欢我的同事们，我们过得很开心，

sentences.en: it's a really nice team, but I was really quite bored of, you know, logging in at 9am, logging out at 5pm and taking customer service calls.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的团队，但我真的对，你知道的，早上9点打卡上班、下午5点打卡下班以及接听客服电话感到非常厌烦。

sentences.en: And so I, so I could log myself out of the system and not be accountable, I would take on Excel spreadsheet duties to look at team performance and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以为了能让自己登出系统又不用承担责任，我会揽下制作Excel电子表格的活儿，去查看团队绩效之类的事情。

sentences.en: Because then my data would be completely skewed, and it would be useless to anybody.
sentences.zh: 因为那样我的数据就会被完全搞砸，对任何人都毫无用处。

sentences.en: But yeah, having something extra to keep myself busy in quite a mundane job, really, because it was,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，在这样一份相当平凡的工作中找点额外的事情来让自己忙碌起来，真的，因为它是，

sentences.en: I guess, in terms of stimulation, I needed more, I needed more, like I needed other stuff to be going
sentences.zh: 我想，就刺激感而言，我需要更多，我需要更多，就像我需要在桌子底下

sentences.en: on under the desk, so that I could sit still in this really boring, repetitive role.
sentences.zh: 搞点别的动静，这样我才能在这个极其无聊、重复的岗位上安坐下来。

sentences.en: I can still say it, good afternoon, store support, Marianne speaking, how can I help?
sentences.zh: 我甚至还能说出这句话：下午好，店铺支援部，玛丽安为您服务，请问有什么可以帮您？

sentences.en: Like, sometimes when I go to pick up the phone, that still wants to come out.
sentences.zh: 就像有时候当我准备去接电话时，那句话还是会脱口而出。

sentences.en: It wasn't enough, I needed, I needed more.
sentences.zh: 这还不够，我需要，我需要更多。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: And again, that's not uncommon, the ADHD brain is often moving quickly, there's lots going through your mind, and doing something mundane isn't enough, it will be looking for more
sentences.zh: 话说回来，这也是很常见的，多动症的大脑通常运转很快，你的脑海里闪过很多想法，做一些平凡的事情是远远不够的，它会寻求比这

sentences.en: than that.
sentences.zh: 更多的刺激。

sentences.en: And so yeah, I mean, it's helpful that you were able to create ways to stay in that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，你能想办法坚持下来，这很有帮助。

sentences.en: But, you know, that's what you might see in the classroom with the child who's always doodling, or the, you know, the child who looks like they're not listening, because they're,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这也就是你在课堂上可能会看到的现象：那个总是在涂鸦的孩子，或者，你知道的，看起来好像没在听讲的孩子，因为他们

sentences.en: you know, kind of doodling, writing, drawing, whatever, they're distracted by something, actually, they're probably looking for more stimulation, because it's not enough,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在涂涂画画、写写画画，或者在干别的，他们被某些东西分心了，但实际上，他们可能是在寻求更多的刺激，因为眼前的还不够，

sentences.en: and their brain is kind of craving more.
sentences.zh: 他们的脑子在渴望更多东西。

sentences.en: So yeah, that's not uncommon.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: And sometimes that is treated negatively as well, you know, always fiddling with pens, always rocking on a chair, you know, never seems to be paying attention, you know,
sentences.zh: 有时这也会被负面看待，你知道的，总是在玩弄钢笔，总是在椅子上晃来晃去，你知道的，好像永远没在专心听讲，你知道的，

sentences.en: staring out the window, looking at this, doing that.
sentences.zh: 望着窗外，看这个，做那个。

sentences.en: Whereas in actual fact, they may still be able to tune into exactly what you're saying, but they're just,
sentences.zh: 然而事实上，他们可能仍然能够准确地捕捉到你所说的话，但他们只是，

sentences.en: you know, doing other things as well, so that they can, I don't know, show you respect, so they can pay attention, but they need, they need more.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，同时还在做别的事情，这样他们才能，怎么说呢，向你表示尊重，以便他们能够集中注意力，但他们需要，他们需要更多。

sentences.en: You know, I think when we're looking at schools, for example, and I'm not talking about children now, but, you know, what behaviours are exhibited when sitting still is expected.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为当我们审视学校时，比如说，我指的现在不是指小孩子们，而是，你知道的，当要求保持坐定静止时会表现出哪些行为。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, I think it's just useful as a question for all of us to think about when I need to sit still.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为，你知道的，我认为这只是一个有用的问题，值得我们所有人思考：当我需要坐着不动时，

sentences.en: Am I right with that?
sentences.zh: 我这样做真的合适吗？

sentences.en: You know, do I need to do other things?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我需要做点别的事情吗？

sentences.en: Do I need to sit like this?
sentences.zh: 我需要这样坐着吗？

sentences.en: Or sit in constrained ways?
sentences.zh: 还是以受束缚的姿势坐着？

sentences.en: Or, you know, rock or fiddle?
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，晃动或者摆弄东西？

sentences.en: That little thing that I fiddle with off the front of my diary here sometimes.
sentences.zh: 就像我有时会摆弄我这里日记本封面上的那个小东西一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, like just having a little look at what it takes for you to show up in the world.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像稍微观察一下你需要付出什么才能在这个世界上表现出自然的自己。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: And I think that's the thing, you know, thinking about children, but also adults in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是关键所在，你知道的，不仅要考虑孩子，还要考虑职场中的成年人。

sentences.en: Actually, the more someone is forced to do it the neurotypical way, or like trying to get someone to sit still, be quiet, do things in line with something that doesn't fit with
sentences.zh: 实际上，一个人越是被迫以神经典型的方式去做事，或者试图让某人坐好、保持安静、按照某种不适合

sentences.en: them, the more you're going to see a child who struggles.
sentences.zh: 他们的规范去做事，你就会看到越多苦苦挣扎的孩子。

sentences.en: And often then, you know, a child might end up being labelled as naughty or difficult, or someone in the workplace might be considered kind
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，你知道的，一个孩子最后可能会被贴上淘气或难管教的标签，或者职场中的某个人会被认为有点

sentences.en: of difficult when actually they're just trying to conform to, you know, standards that don't fit and
sentences.zh: 难相处，而实际上他们只是在试图顺应那些不适合他们、

sentences.en: don't work for them, rather than being able to adjust and think, ah, what what does someone need?
sentences.zh: 对他们不管用的标准，而不是能够去调整并思考，啊，一个人到底需要什么？

sentences.en: You know, the children often in the classroom, it might be like, right, can they do a few laps of the
sentences.zh: 你知道的，课堂上的孩子们通常可能会被要求，好，他们能不能去操场上跑上

sentences.en: playground because they need to burn off a bit of energy before they're able to then sit still and to be able to listen?
sentences.zh: 几圈，因为他们需要消耗掉一些精力，然后才能坐下来听讲？

sentences.en: Or so, yeah, I think that's really important to think about accommodations.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为思考无障碍适应措施真的很重要。

sentences.en: If you want someone to be able to thrive rather than labelling them as, you know, kind of naughty or not doing what they're told, as if it's a kind of conscious choice.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让一个人能够蓬勃发展，而不是给他们贴上，你知道的，诸如淘气或不听话的标签，好像这是某种有意识的选择一样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Can we think about what people's options might be if they did want to explore an ADHD diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 我们能想想如果人们真的想探索自己是否患有多动症（ADHD），可能会有哪些选择吗？

sentences.en: I'm guessing most areas of the country will have some sort of NHS provision.
sentences.zh: 我猜全国大多数地区都会有一些国民保健制度（NHS）的医疗服务。

sentences.en: Is there a right to choose pathway?
sentences.zh: 是不是有一个“自主选择权”（Right to Choose）的绿色通道？

sentences.en: And then, of course, private options as well.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然也有私立的选择。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if you are considering an ADHD assessment for you or for your child, the first step, if you want to go down a kind of NHS route would be to contact your GP surgery.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你正在考虑为你自己或你的孩子进行多动症评估，第一步，如果你想走国民保健制度（NHS）的路线，就是联系你的全科医生（GP）诊所。

sentences.en: Most
sentences.zh: 大多数

sentences.en: GPs will ask you to fill in.
sentences.zh: 全科医生会要求你填写表格。

sentences.en: There are different questionnaires, depending on if it's an adult or child and different practices have a different one.
sentences.zh: 根据是成年人还是儿童，会有不同的问卷，不同的诊所使用的问卷也不同。

sentences.en: So check with your GP, but they normally do like a screening questionnaire to look at, does it look like there are symptoms present?
sentences.zh: 所以请向你的全科医生确认，但他们通常会做一个类似筛查的问卷，来查看：是否存在相关症状？

sentences.en: And then you can be referred for a assessment in your kind of local NHS team.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以被转诊到你当地的国民保健制度团队进行评估。

sentences.en: As long as they feel you kind of meet the criteria.
sentences.zh: 只要他们觉得你符合相关标准。

sentences.en: In some areas of the country, the wait is about five years for that.
sentences.zh: 在全国某些地区，这方面的等待时间大约是五年。

sentences.en: It varies depending on where you are, but actually the weights for NHS assessments are quite big at the moment.
sentences.zh: 具体时间取决于你所在的地区，但实际上目前国民保健制度评估的等待时间非常长。

sentences.en: Now we know more and more about how it presents and more and more adults are looking back and realising that they've always had it.
sentences.zh: 现在我们对它的表现形式有了越来越多的了解，越来越多的成年人开始回首过去，并意识到自己一直都有这种状况。

sentences.en: So yeah, they're quite long wait lists.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，等待名单相当长。

sentences.en: There is a right to choose pathway, as you mentioned, and that's the
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，确实存在“自主选择权”通道，而且

sentences.en: same for children as well, which is, you can choose a provider that's a private provider that is funded by the NHS.
sentences.zh: 这对儿童来说也是一样的，也就是说，你可以选择一个由国民保健制度（NHS）资助的私立医疗机构。

sentences.en: So there will be some private options.
sentences.zh: 所以会有一些私立的选择。

sentences.en: So it's worth asking your GP surgery, they might say, okay, there's only a two year wait list instead of a five year on right to choose.
sentences.zh: 因此，向你的全科医生诊所询问是很有价值的，他们可能会说，好吧，通过“自主选择权”只需要等待两年，而不是五年。

sentences.en: Some areas, it's quite fast, some areas, it's not, it is a real postcode lottery.
sentences.zh: 在某些地区，速度相当快；在另一些地区则不然，这真是一场看邮政编码运气的彩票。

sentences.en: So you can go down the right to choose kind of option.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以选择“自主选择权”这种方案。

sentences.en: Again, if you think a child might have autistic traits, as well as
sentences.zh: 同样，如果你认为一个孩子可能既有自闭症特质，又有

sentences.en: ADHD, you might want to look carefully at the providers that they give you a choice of, because some will do both and some won't.
sentences.zh: 多动症，你可能需要仔细查看他们让你选择的医疗机构，因为有些机构两者都能评估，而有些则不能。

sentences.en: So you might find that you pick a provider and actually they don't have a full understanding of, say, autism, and that affects how they feel about the assessments.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会发现你选了一个机构，但实际上他们对，比方说自闭症并没有充分的理解，这会影响他们对评估结果的看法。

sentences.en: That's something to look at.
sentences.zh: 这是需要注意的一点。

sentences.en: And then some people will say, actually, the wait is too long, my child needs to have an assessment before that.
sentences.zh: 然后有些人会说，实际上，等待时间太长了，我的孩子需要在那之前接受评估。

sentences.en: For example, I think you need to, sorry, I don't remember, I think it's two years before someone's GCSEs, they have to have a diagnosis in place to have any accommodations
sentences.zh: 例如，我认为你需要，抱歉，我记不太清了，好像是在一个人参加普通中等教育证书（GCSE）考试的两年前，他们必须确诊并拥有诊断证明，才能在

sentences.en: in their GCSE exaMs. So for some people, they might notice tendencies in their child, their child might
sentences.zh: 普通中等教育证书考试中获得任何便利 accommodations（调整措施）。所以对有些人来说，他们可能会注意到自己孩子身上的倾向，他们的孩子可能

sentences.en: be struggling, and the wait list means that they would then not get accommodations in exams, like extra time or someone reading out the questions or things that would support them.
sentences.zh: 正在苦苦挣扎，而漫长的等待名单意味着他们将无法在考试中获得便利，比如延长时间、安排专人朗读题目或提供其他支持他们的措施。

sentences.en: So they might say, I don't want to wait that long, or I can't wait that long, it's impacting well-being, and they might choose to go
sentences.zh: 因此他们可能会说，我不想等那么久，或者我等不了那么久，这已经影响到了身心健康，于是他们可能会选择

sentences.en: privately instead, or they might feel more confident in a private diagnosis, being more holistic.
sentences.zh: 转而寻求私立医疗，或者他们会觉得私立诊断更加全面，从而更有信心。

sentences.en: And so yeah, some people might choose then to go private.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，有些人可能会选择去私立机构。

sentences.en: And again, you've got bigger companies that might do sorter and lower cost assessments, and then you've got more kind of individuals that
sentences.zh: 同样，有些规模较大的公司可能会提供更快捷、成本更低的评估，然后还有更多类型的个人专家，

sentences.en: specialize in it, that might do a more in-depth and kind of personalized assessment.
sentences.zh: 他们专门从事这方面工作，可能会提供更深入、更个性化的评估。

sentences.en: It is worth thinking if people are wondering about medication, if you go for right to choose or private, sometimes that will be accepted by your GP, sometimes it won't.
sentences.zh: 如果人们对药物治疗感到好奇，值得考虑的是，如果你选择“自主选择权”或私立途径，有时你的全科医生会接受，有时则不会。

sentences.en: Even if your GP says, go with this provider from right to choose, they might then say, we're not accepting shared care to pay for medication.
sentences.zh: 即使你的全科医生说，去选“自主选择权”名单上的这个机构吧，他们之后也可能会说：我们不接受用于支付药费的共享护理（shared care）方案。

sentences.en: But other GPs will take it, it's not an absolute no.
sentences.zh: 但其他全科医生会接受，这并不是绝对的“不”。

sentences.en: So it is worth speaking, every GP has their own rules, they can make up their own rules on whether they accept shared care or not.
sentences.zh: 所以这很值得沟通，每个全科医生都有他们自己的规则，他们可以自行决定是否接受共享护理。

sentences.en: So it literally varies.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的因人而异、变化多端。

sentences.en: And sometimes people might have a diagnosis, their GP says, no, I won't accept shared care, and they ring up the other GP in their area 10 minutes down the road.
sentences.zh: 有时人们可能已经确诊了，全科医生说，不，我不会接受共享护理，于是他们给他们地区内几分钟车程外的另一家全科医生诊所打电话。

sentences.en: And they say, oh, we do.
sentences.zh: 对方说，哦，我们接受。

sentences.en: And so they just swap GP surgeries.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就直接换了全科医生诊所。

sentences.en: So sometimes it's as simple as, you know, kind of exploring in the area.
sentences.zh: 所以有时事情就是这么简单，你知道的，也就是在当地多了解打听一下。

sentences.en: But yeah, in terms of medication privately, you might be able to access a prescriber through the kind of, so when we do assessments, we're on a prescriber pathway, which means our
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，就私立药物治疗而言，你或许可以通过某种途径联系到开处方的人，所以，当我们进行评估时，我们处于开处方者的路径上，这意味着我们

sentences.en: reports, any reports done within the practice are accepted to be of a quality standard.
sentences.zh: 诊所出具的报告，以及诊所内完成的任何报告，都被认为达到了质量标准。

sentences.en: And a prescriber will look and be able to kind of prescribe medication.
sentences.zh: 并且开处方者会进行评估，并能够开具相应的药物。

sentences.en: And if you get medication privately, again, you might be able to then stabilise on a dose and go back to your GP and say, will you take over shared care?
sentences.zh: 如果你通过私立途径获得了药物，同样，你也许能够将剂量稳定下来，然后回到你的全科医生那里说：你们愿意接手共享护理吗？

sentences.en: So there are lots of options, it is a bit confusing.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多选择，这确实有点让人眼花缭乱。

sentences.en: Children's assessments tend to be better done face to face.
sentences.zh: 儿童评估往往最好是面对面进行。

sentences.en: So I would recommend getting someone local who does it face to face rather than online for children's assessments.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于儿童评估，我建议找当地能面对面做评估的人，而不是在线上进行。

sentences.en: For adults' assessments, it's okay to do online, as long as they meet the other kind of guidelines.
sentences.zh: 对于成人的评估，只要符合其他相关指南，在线做是可以的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: That's really interesting, really helpful for people to kind of take on board and consider their options.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有意思，对大家吸收这些信息并考虑自己的选择非常有帮助。

sentences.en: I know, you know, it's probably quite a big question with perhaps quite a lot of range.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这可能是一个相当大的问题，涉及的范围也很广。

sentences.en: But if someone's looking into, for example, a private ADHD assessment for an adult, is there a sign of a price range for that that people might be able to expect?
sentences.zh: 但如果有人在了解例如成人私立ADHD评估，大家大概可以预期一个什么样的价格范围呢？

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, but it does depend.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，会的，但这取决于具体情况。

sentences.en: It depends on how someone prices it.
sentences.zh: 这取决于收费标准。

sentences.en: So there is quite a range sometimes in how long an assessment will take.
sentences.zh: 因此，评估需要多长时间，有时价格跨度还是蛮大的。

sentences.en: If you go in depth with someone, if someone has had a lot of difficult life experiences, or it's more complex, it's going to be a longer assessment.
sentences.zh: 如果你和评估师深入交流，如果有人经历过很多生活难关，或者情况比较复杂，评估时间就会更长。

sentences.en: So some people will price an ADHD assessment as a kind of a one off fee, they might say, okay, it's 1000
sentences.zh: 所以有些人会将ADHD评估定价为一次性打包费用，他们可能会说，好吧，是1000

sentences.en: pounds, or it's 1500 pounds, or, you know, kind of, you might get a one off kind of bulk price, other people might say it depends on the length of the assessment.
sentences.zh: 英镑，或者是1500英镑，你知道的，你可能会得到一个一次性的打包价格，而另一些人则会说这取决于评估的时长。

sentences.en: So within our practice, we do it by an hourly rate, because that means that for some people, otherwise, they will be paying a high fee, and
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的诊所里，我们是按小时收费的，因为这意味着对某些人来说，否则他们就要支付很高的费用，而

sentences.en: they're not requiring that amount of time, it feels really unfair for them.
sentences.zh: 他们并不需要那么多时间，这让他们觉得很不公平。
